lectures.title: Time and Space Complexity of Circular Singly Linked List

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture, we will combine all the methods that we have created for circle Single Linked List
together and to see the big picture of time and space complexity.
Now the first method is create method.
Now here take into account that we are creating the empty linked list.
That's why the space and time complexity is going to be zero one.
Then we have append method.
Append method appends element to the beginning of circle single linked list.
So here we are just updating the header pointers.
That's why the time and space complex is going to be zero one and prepend method adds nodes at the end
of the linked list.
So here again we are updating the next reference of tail pointer to point to this newly created node
and this newly created node's next reference to point to the first node.
That's why the time and space complexity is going to be zero one.
Then we have insert method.
Now insert method inserts at a specified location in the linked list.
That's why we need to find out that location.
Here we have a loop.
So in the worst case it will take o n time complexity.
Then the space complexity is going to be o one.
Now search method uses the linear approach.
That's why search method takes o n time complexity and space complexity.
Here again is o one.
Now when it comes to the Traversing.
Traversing means that we are visiting all nodes of the linked list one by one.
That's why the time complexity is going to be o n space complexity is o one.
Now, when it comes to the get method, get method also uses the linear approach.
So we know that linear approach takes the o n time complexity.
Now when we are using the set method we are using the get method.
That's why the time complexity here again it is on.
Now when it comes to the Pope, first we are using the assignment statements over here.
That's why the time complexity is O one and the space complexity is O one.
Now Pope method takes time complexity of o n, because here we have to loop through the elements to
find the second last node.
Then we have remove method.
So here again based on the index we have to find the node.
That's why the time complexity is going to be n.
Now when we are deleting all elements from the circular single linked list, we are just updating the
head and tail and last nodes.
Next reference.
That's why the time complexity is o one and the space complexity is O one, because an additional memory
is not required to perform this operation.
So hopefully with this lecture you have a big picture of time and space complexity of a single linked
list.
And with this lecture we have come to the end of this section and hopefully everything is clear.
